title: Ordinary inverse-image and balanced scalar-tower square
statement:
Let $h:\operatorname{Sh}(C_X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(C_Y)$ be a morphism of topoi, on sites small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, def-weil-size-convention], and let $A_Y\xrightarrow{a}B_Y\xrightarrow{b}C_Y$ be commutative ring sheaves. On $X$ take their inverse images and maps. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and sheafified balanced tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $r\to s$ put $E_{rs}^V=s_V\otimes_{r_V}-$, with its first-factor action, and let $h_r^*$ mean inverse image of $r_Y$-modules. Let
$$\chi_h^{rs}:h_s^*E_{rs}^Y\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{rs}^Xh_r^*$$
be the comparison of the balanced coequalizers: inverse image of the scalar and module action arrows is identified with the corresponding pair over $X$. Let
$$t_V:E_{BC}^VE_{AB}^V\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{AC}^V,\qquad c\otimes(b'\otimes m)\mapsto c\,b(b')\otimes m$$
be scalar reassociation, inverse to $c\otimes m\mapsto c\otimes(1\otimes m)$. Then the following equality holds as natural transformations of $C_X$-module sheaves:
$$\chi_h^{AC}\circ h_C^*(t_Y)=(t_Xh_A^*)\circ E_{BC}^X(\chi_h^{AB})\circ(\chi_h^{BC}E_{AB}^Y).$$
The equality also holds termwise on cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This statement concerns the specified balanced quotient maps, with their coefficient actions, and asserts no derived-functor existence or K-flat preservation.

proof.text: Identify restriction along b followed by restriction along a with restriction along a;b, using the sectionwise restriction-of-scalars composition isomorphism. Uniqueness of left adjoints to this composite restriction functor gives scalar reassociation. The left-adjoint uniqueness unit equation gives t(1 tensor (1 tensor m))=1 tensor m. Scalar linearity and the inner balancing relation give t(c tensor (s tensor m))=(c*b(s)) tensor m. Applying the inverse of t gives the inverse insertion formula. All maps are natural module morphisms; neither flatness nor generation by global sections is used.

Construct the module direct-image functor P for B_Y and B_X by geometric module transport. Its underlying sheaf is V, and its addition and scalar action obey the transported operation equations. For the supplied presentation I_A, the underlying sheaf adjunction restricts to a natural bijection Hom_AX(I_A M, Res_aX H) = Hom_AY(M, Res_aY P H): addition and scalar linearity correspond under the binary mate equations, and the scalar condition uses the given compatibility of a_Y with a_X. For identity coefficient arrows the same construction gives I_B left adjoint to P. Compose the scalar adjunction with these natural Hom bijections. Both E_aY;I_B and I_A;E_aX are left adjoint to P;Res_aY. Left-adjoint uniqueness gives their comparison e. Its defining Hom equation, followed by the faithful underlying-sheaf functor and the normalized geometric Hom bijection, says e F(u_aY)=u_aX. For an arbitrary generalized pure tensor z=s*u_aY(m), the graph equation for I_B transports this scalar action, and B_X-linearity of e gives precisely the required pure-tensor normalization. Apply this construction to A to B and B to C.

Define the A to C comparison by pasting inverse reassociation over Y, the B to C comparison, extension of the A to B comparison, and reassociation over X. To check its normalization on arbitrary generalized sections, inverse reassociation takes c tensor m to c tensor (1 tensor m). The B to C comparison transports the outer scalar and inner unit. The A to B comparison sends the transported inner unit to 1 tensor m, since the ring presentation preserves 1. Extension of scalars acts on the inner module map, and reassociation over X takes c tensor (1 tensor m) to c tensor m. Naturality of the supplied underlying-sheaf isomorphisms justifies each transport; no pointwise generation assertion is required.

The natural-transformation square follows by cancelling the inverse and forward Y reassociation in the definition of the A to C comparison, using functoriality of I_C. Evaluating this equality at the object K.X n of any cochain complex gives exactly the requested termwise equality.
